explainer_content.short_definition: A late-1960s pop-rock road where hooks, harmonies, studio effects, and counterculture color make familiar song forms feel unreal.
explainer_content.history_capsule: Psychedelic pop is not only long jams and acid-rock heaviness. The Beatles, Beach Boys, Turtles, Monkees, Jefferson Airplane, and others brought dream logic into singles: odd timbres, tape edits, surreal images, bright harmonies, and arrangements that seem to open hidden rooms.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It made experimental studio craft safe for pop radio and gave later art pop, indie psych, and studio maximalism a colorful ancestor.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: Compared with heavy psych, this lane keeps melodic accessibility. Compared with baroque pop, it is more hallucinatory and rhythmically open.
what_to_listen_for: Tape effects, varispeed, or unusual transitions
A hook that returns after an unexpected detour
